title: C. B. Facey Foundation Grants 2026: Funding Opportunities for Arts, Education and Environmental Initiatives in Jamaica
summary: The C. B. Facey Foundation provides funding and support for initiatives that contribute to the development of communities through its mandated areas of Arts, Education and the Environment . The Foundation accepts grant applications during a specific annual application period, while sponsorship and ticket purchase requests can be submitted throughout the year for consideration. For organizations, community groups, institutions and other eligible applicants working within the Foundation s areas of interest, this presents an opportunity to seek financial support for initiatives that align with the Foundation s mandate. About the C. B. Facey Foundation The C. B. Facey Foundation supports activities and initiatives within three principal areas: Arts Education Environment Its support is structured through different avenues, including annual grant applications, sponsorship requests and specific scholarship arrangements. Applicants should understand that these avenues have different application procedures and timelines. In particular, the annual grant application period should not be confused with sponsorship requests, which can be submitted year-round. C. B. Facey Foundation Grant Applications The Foundation accepts grant applications annually from August 12 to October 12 . This annual application window provides an opportunity for applicants seeking financial support for eligible initiatives to submit their proposals for consideration. Application period The annual grant application period is: Opening date: August 12 Deadline: October 12 each year APPLY HERE Applicants interested in receiving grant support should therefore prepare their proposals and supporting information before the application period opens. Because applications are only accepted during the specified annual period, applicants should pay close attention to the dates and ensure that their submissions are made within the Foundation s designated window. Areas Covered by the Foundation The Foundation s mandate covers three major areas: Arts, Education and the Environment. 1. Arts Organizations and initiatives working within the arts may fall within one of the Foundation s areas of interest. This may include activities connected to artistic and cultural development, although the information provided does not specify a complete list of eligible arts projects or the maximum amount that can be requested. Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed initiative clearly demonstrates its relevance to the Foundation s arts mandate. 2. Education Education is another core area supported by the C. B. Facey Foundation. Applicants seeking support for education-related initiatives should ensure that their proposals demonstrate a clear connection to educational development and fall within the Foundation s mandated areas. The Foundation also provides scholarships through specific educational institutions, but these scholarships operate separately from the general grant application process. 3. Environment Environmental initiatives are also included within the Foundation s mandate. However, applicants should distinguish between the Foundation s general grant applications and the Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant , which is specifically intended for conservation projects. Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant The Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant Application is designed for conservation projects. According to the information provided, the Eco-Grant application is currently closed . This means applicants interested specifically in conservation funding should not assume that the general C. B. Facey Foundation grant application period automatically applies to the Eco-Grant. Those interested in future conservation funding opportunities should monitor the relevant application announcements for information about when the Eco-Grant reopens. Sponsorship Opportunities The C. B. Facey Foundation also considers sponsorship and ticket purchase requests separately from its annual grant applications. Unlike the annual grants, sponsorship and ticket purchase requests can be submitted year-round . Requests must fall within the Foundation s mandated areas of: Arts Education Environment Applicants or organizations seeking sponsorship should submit their requests by email to: cbfacey@panjamaica.com This means organizations do not necessarily have to wait until the August 12 to October 12 grant application period to request sponsorship or ticket purchase support. However, submitting a request does not guarantee funding or sponsorship. Requests are subject to consideration by the Foundation. How Sponsorship Requests Work Those seeking sponsorship or requesting ticket purchases should prepare their request clearly and explain the purpose of the support being sought. A strong request should make it easy for the Foundation to understand: Who is making the request. What activity, event or initiative is being proposed. Whether the request relates to Arts, Education or the Environment. What type of sponsorship or ticket purchase support is being requested. Why the initiative is relevant to the Foundation s mandate. The Foundation can then consider the request based on its own criteria and priorities. Scholarship Opportunities The C. B. Facey Foundation also provides scholarships, but these scholarships are not open through a general Foundation application process . The Foundation specifically states that it grants scholarships only to: Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture This is an important distinction for prospective applicants. Students interested in these scholarships must apply through the bursaries of the respective institutions . Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts Students interested in scholarships associated with the Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts should contact and apply through the institution s bursary. Applicants should not send a separate scholarship application directly to the C. B. Facey Foundation unless specifically instructed to do so. UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture Students interested in scholarships associated with the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture must similarly apply through the institution s bursary. The Foundation s information does not indicate that these scholarships are available to students at other universities or colleges. Important Difference Between Grants, Sponsorships and Scholarships Applicants should understand the differences between the Foundation s support mechanisms. Support Type Application Period Main Areas/Recipients General Grants August 12 – October 12 annually Arts, Education and Environment Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant Currently closed Conservation projects Sponsorships/Ticket Purchases Year-round Arts, Education and Environment Scholarships Through respective institutions Edna Manley College and UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture This distinction is important because each opportunity follows a different process. For example, someone seeking funding for an eligible organizational project may need to use the annual grant application process, while someone seeking event sponsorship can submit a request by email throughout the year. Similarly, a student seeking one of the Foundation s scholarships should approach the relevant institution s bursary rather than submitting a general scholarship application to the Foundation. Deadline for C. B. Facey Foundation Grant Applications The annual grant application deadline is: October 12 each year The application period begins on August 12 . Applicants should therefore make sure that their applications are submitted before October 12 rather than waiting until the final day. For sponsorship and ticket purchase requests, there is no annual deadline , as requests can be emailed year-round. The Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant is currently closed. How to Contact the C. B. Facey Foundation Applicants and interested individuals who have questions or concerns can contact the Foundation directly. Email: cbfacey@panjamaica.com Telephone: 876-929-4510 The email address can be used for questions relating to grants, sponsorships, ticket purchase requests and other matters within the Foundation s mandate. Visit HERE to learn more about the C. B. Facey Foundation Grants 2026 Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be relevant to organizations, initiatives and applicants working within the Foundation s stated areas of interest. Potential applicants include those involved in: Arts and cultural initiatives Educational initiatives Environmental initiatives Conservation-related projects, when the relevant Eco-Grant is open Events or activities seeking sponsorship within the Foundation s mandated areas Students should note that the scholarship component is much more specific. According to the information provided, scholarships are limited to students applying through the bursaries of Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts and the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture . What Applicants Should Keep in Mind Before submitting a request, applicants should first determine which type of support best matches their needs. If you are seeking grant funding , check whether your initiative fits within Arts, Education or the Environment and prepare your application for the August 12–October 12 annual window. If you are seeking sponsorship or ticket purchases , you can submit your request by email at any time during the year. If you are seeking a scholarship , confirm whether you are applying through one of the two institutions identified by the Foundation and submit your application through the appropriate bursary. If your project is specifically focused on conservation , be aware that the Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant is currently closed and that a separate announcement may be required when applications reopen. Conclusion The C. B. Facey Foundation offers several forms of support for initiatives connected to Arts, Education and the Environment . Its main grant application period runs annually from August 12 to October 12 , giving eligible applicants a defined window in which to seek grant funding. Beyond the annual grant programme, the Foundation accepts sponsorship and ticket purchase requests throughout the year by email. Meanwhile, its scholarship support is specifically directed to students at Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts and the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture , with applications handled through the respective institutions bursaries. Applicants should carefully identify the appropriate funding route before submitting a request and ensure that their initiative falls within the Foundation s stated areas of support. Deadline for annual grant applications: October 12 each year. Contact: cbfacey@panjamaica.com | 876-929-4510 For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org. title: Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028: 10-Week Residency in France for Artists, Scholars and Thinkers
summary: The Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 is now accepting applications from established and mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers seeking dedicated time and space for research, experimentation, reflection, and creative development. Created in 1971 by Jerome Hill , the Camargo Fellowship is the flagship residency program of the Camargo Foundation , based in Cassis, France. Over the decades, the Foundation has supported more than 1,500 individuals through its residency programs. The 2027–2028 call offers residencies taking place in Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 , giving selected fellows an opportunity to spend approximately 10 weeks in an environment designed to encourage independent work, interdisciplinary exchange, artistic creation, and research. The Camargo Foundation describes its residency environment as a space where artists, scholars, and researchers can step away from their normal routines and dedicate focused time to developing their work. The Foundation s current information also highlights its long-standing role in supporting artistic and intellectual exploration on the Mediterranean coast of France. What Is the Camargo Fellowship? The Camargo Fellowship is the Camargo Foundation s flagship residency program, established in 1971 by Jerome Hill. The program is designed to provide selected artists, scholars, and thinkers with the time, space, and conditions necessary for independent and rigorous work . Rather than functioning like a conventional academic scholarship or employment opportunity, the fellowship is structured around a residency model. During the residency, fellows can dedicate themselves to: Research Artistic creation Experimentation Writing and intellectual work Reflection Development of new ideas Interdisciplinary exchange Exploration of new approaches to their practice or research The Foundation s mission emphasizes supporting artistic creation and research in their various forms while encouraging exchange between different fields of knowledge. Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Residency Period The current call is for residencies taking place during: Fall 2027 Spring 2028 Each residency lasts approximately 10 weeks . This period gives fellows an extended opportunity to step away from their usual professional or academic environment and concentrate on a particular project, research question, creative practice, or intellectual investigation. Who Is the Camargo Fellowship Designed For? The fellowship is intended for established or mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers from diverse backgrounds . The opportunity therefore extends across multiple fields rather than focusing exclusively on one artistic discipline or academic subject. Potential applicants may include professionals working in areas such as: Visual arts Literature and writing Performing arts Cultural research Humanities Social sciences Other forms of scholarly or intellectual inquiry Interdisciplinary artistic and research practices The important consideration is that applicants should have an established or mid-career practice and a meaningful project or area of research that can benefit from a dedicated residency period. What Can Fellows Use the Residency For? The Camargo Fellowship provides a setting for research, experimentation, and reflection . This means that the residency can be valuable for people who need concentrated time to develop work that may be difficult to pursue alongside their normal professional responsibilities. For an artist, this could mean using the residency to develop a new body of work, explore a new creative approach, or deepen an existing artistic project. For a scholar, it could provide time for research, writing, analysis, or development of a major intellectual project. For a thinker or interdisciplinary practitioner, it could provide an opportunity to investigate ideas that connect different areas of knowledge and practice. The Foundation s broader mission is particularly focused on encouraging exchange across different fields and supporting independent, rigorous, and emancipatory work. A Unique Opportunity for Focused Work One of the major advantages of a residency such as the Camargo Fellowship is the opportunity to dedicate substantial time to a project without the same day-to-day pressures that can accompany normal professional or academic life. The Foundation describes its residency environment as providing artists and scholars with an opportunity to recharge, create, and collaborate , while also offering space for personal reflection. The 10-week residency can therefore be particularly useful for applicants who have reached a stage in their work where concentrated time and a supportive environment could help them make significant progress. The Camargo Foundation s International Community The Camargo Foundation has developed an international community of artists, researchers, and thinkers throughout its history. The Foundation s 2025 figures, for example, indicate that it hosted 54 artists, researchers, and thinkers in residence , representing 18 countries and five continents . This international environment is an important part of the broader residency experience. Fellows have opportunities to work independently while also being situated within a community that brings together people working across different disciplines, cultures, and perspectives. Why Interdisciplinary Exchange Matters The Camargo Fellowship is not only about giving fellows a physical place to work. The Foundation s mission places considerable emphasis on exchange across different fields of knowledge . Bringing artists, scholars, researchers, and thinkers together can create opportunities for people to encounter perspectives outside their usual areas of specialization. This can encourage: New research questions. New creative approaches. Cross-disciplinary collaboration. Intellectual exchange. Broader perspectives on existing work. Development of ideas that connect different fields. For applicants whose work sits between disciplines, this environment may be particularly valuable. Important Change to the Camargo Fellowship Application Process One of the most important pieces of information for prospective applicants is that the 2026 open call is expected to be the last public open call under the current system . According to the Foundation s announcement, beginning in July 2027 , it plans to introduce a new selection process that will no longer be based on a public open call . This makes the current application round particularly significant for artists, scholars, and thinkers who are considering applying for a Camargo residency. The Foundation explains that the change is intended to broaden the diversity of profiles welcomed into residence and create opportunities for a wider range of: Practices Perspectives Research themes Creative approaches The Foundation also connects this change to its broader commitment to keeping its mission relevant and renewed. APPLY HERE Why Applicants Should Consider Applying Now Because of the planned change to the selection process, people who are interested in completing a Camargo residency should consider the 2027–2028 call as an important opportunity . The current public call provides applicants with an opportunity to apply directly through the established application process. After the new selection system begins in July 2027, prospective applicants will no longer be able to rely on the same public open-call model. Therefore, artists, scholars, and thinkers who have been considering the Camargo Fellowship should carefully review the current eligibility requirements and submit an application if they believe their work aligns with the program. Application Period Applications for the 2027–2028 Camargo Fellowship opened on: July 2, 2026 The application period runs through: September 30, 2026 The supplied announcement also identifies October 1, 2026 as the deadline. Applicants should therefore submit their applications before the stated deadline and should verify the exact closing time displayed on the official application platform before submitting. How to Apply for the Camargo Fellowship Applicants interested in the 2027–2028 residency should complete the application through the Camargo Foundation s online submission platform. The official application platform is hosted through Submittable . Camargo Foundation application platform Applicants should carefully review the fellowship guidelines before beginning the application. The Foundation s official website provides dedicated sections for applying and reviewing residency conditions. Review the Fellowship Guidelines Before Applying The Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Guidelines contain important information concerning the residency conditions and eligibility requirements. Applicants should use the guidelines to confirm that: They meet the eligibility requirements. Their professional level is appropriate for the fellowship. Their proposed project aligns with the purpose of the residency. They understand the residency duration. They understand the financial and practical conditions. They have the required application materials. They understand what is expected during the residency. Because residency opportunities can have specific requirements that are not always captured in a short announcement, applicants should read the complete guidelines before submitting their application. Residency Environment The Camargo Foundation is located in Cassis, France , on the Mediterranean coast. The Foundation s current materials describe the location as an environment where artists and scholars can find space to reflect, create, and collaborate. The physical setting is part of the broader residency experience, providing fellows with an environment away from the distractions of their usual routines. The Foundation s location, combined with its interdisciplinary community, is intended to create conditions that encourage focused work and exchange. Webinar for Prospective Applicants The Foundation has also provided a webinar for people interested in the fellowship. Prospective applicants can use the webinar to better understand the program and the application process. Applicants should consider watching the session before preparing their application, particularly if they are unfamiliar with residency programs or the Camargo Fellowship. What Makes the Camargo Fellowship Significant? The Camargo Fellowship has operated for more than five decades. Since its establishment in 1971, the Camargo Foundation has supported more than 1,500 individuals through its flagship fellowship program, according to the opportunity announcement. The Foundation s broader recent figures also demonstrate its international reach, with residents representing multiple countries and continents. The longevity of the program means that the fellowship is part of an established international residency tradition rather than being a newly created opportunity. What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying Before submitting an application, prospective fellows should think carefully about what they want to accomplish during the residency. A strong application should clearly communicate the value of having dedicated residency time for the applicant s work. Applicants should consider questions such as: What project or research do I want to develop? Why is this particular period of residency important for my work? What can I realistically accomplish during 10 weeks? How does the proposed work relate to my existing practice or research? What new ideas or approaches do I want to explore? How could the Camargo environment contribute to the development of my work? What makes this stage of my career appropriate for the fellowship? Thinking through these questions can help applicants present a clear and convincing case for their proposed residency. Visit HERE to learn more about the Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Key Details Opportunity: Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Organization: Camargo Foundation Established: 1971 Founder: Jerome Hill Location: Cassis, France Residency length: 10 weeks Residency periods: Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 Target applicants: Established and mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers Purpose: Research, experimentation, reflection, artistic creation, and intellectual work Applications open: July 2, 2026 Application deadline: September 30, 2026 / October 1, 2026 as stated in the supplied announcement Application platform: Camargo Foundation Submittable Future selection change: From July 2027, selection will no longer be based on a public open call Conclusion The Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 offers established and mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers an opportunity to dedicate approximately 10 weeks to research, experimentation, reflection, and creative or intellectual development in Cassis, France. Established in 1971 by Jerome Hill, the Camargo Fellowship has a long history of supporting individuals working across artistic, academic, and intellectual fields. The Foundation s current international residency community demonstrates the program s ability to bring together people from different countries, disciplines, and perspectives. The 2027–2028 call is especially significant because the Foundation has announced that this year s public open call will, until further notice, be the last one under the current application model . From July 2027, a new selection process will replace the public open call. Artists, scholars, and thinkers who have been considering a Camargo residency should therefore take advantage of the current application round and carefully review the official guidelines before submitting their application. Deadline: September 30, 2026, with the supplied announcement also stating October 1, 2026. Applicants should verify the exact closing time on the official application platform before submission. title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University 2027: Fully Funded Innovation and Technology Master’s Scholarship for African Students
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University (ASU) is offering fully funded graduate scholarship opportunities for young African professionals seeking to pursue master’s degrees in technology, innovation, engineering, data science, computing, sustainable energy and related fields in the United States. For the 2027–2028 academic year , the Innovation and Technology Scholarship is offering 30 graduate study opportunities to eligible African students admitted through the scholarship selection process. The programme is designed to provide not only financial support for graduate education but also leadership development, mentorship, professional development, community engagement and other forms of academic and career support. The scholarship provides an opportunity to undertake a full-time, two-year, in-person graduate degree at Arizona State University’s Tempe campus in Arizona, USA . The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ASU describes its current third phase as focused on preparing young African leaders with skills and knowledge in technology and sustainable innovation. Application Deadline: Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT Applicants interested in this opportunity should carefully review the eligibility requirements, degree options, scholarship coverage and application instructions before submitting their applications. About the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global initiative designed to expand access to higher education for talented young people who have the potential to become transformative leaders. At Arizona State University, the partnership has operated through different phases. The current phase, known as Phase III: Innovation and Technology , focuses particularly on technology, innovation and entrepreneurship and provides pathways through graduate education, professional learning and related opportunities. The broader ASU programme is built around more than simply paying for a student s education. Scholars receive holistic support intended to help them succeed academically, professionally and personally. The programme places significant emphasis on leadership development, community engagement and the expectation that scholars will use their knowledge and skills to contribute to positive social and economic development in their communities and home countries. For the 2027–2028 Innovation and Technology Scholarship cycle, selected scholars will have the opportunity to study in technology- and innovation-related master s programmes at ASU. What Makes the 2027 Innovation and Technology Scholarship Important? Graduate education in highly specialised areas such as computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, robotics, information technology and sustainable energy can be expensive, particularly for international students studying in the United States. This scholarship is designed to remove many of those financial barriers by providing comprehensive support to selected scholars. The programme is therefore particularly relevant to young African professionals who have demonstrated: Strong academic achievement Leadership potential Commitment to community service An interest in technology, innovation or sustainable development A desire to use advanced education to contribute to positive change in Africa and beyond The programme s emphasis is not only on what applicants have achieved academically but also on the impact they hope to create through their education and leadership. The official ASU programme describes the scholarship as an opportunity for young African professionals to pursue master s degrees focused on technology and innovation, with women, refugees and displaced persons, and people with disabilities strongly encouraged to apply. Number of Scholarships Available For the 2027–2028 academic year, the programme is offering: 30 graduate study opportunities. These opportunities are intended for eligible African applicants seeking to pursue selected full-time, on-campus master s programmes at Arizona State University. The current ASU Innovation and Technology Scholarship page confirms the availability of 30 graduate study opportunities for the 2027–2028 cycle. Study Location Successful scholars will undertake their graduate studies at: Arizona State University Tempe, Arizona, United States This is an in-person, on-campus programme . Applicants must therefore be prepared to relocate to Tempe and reside on the ASU campus for the duration of their programme. This is important because the opportunity is not simply an online scholarship. Applicants must be able to participate in the traditional campus-based graduate experience. Master s Degree Programmes Covered by the Scholarship The scholarship is available for selected full-time, on-campus graduate programmes in technology, computing, engineering, energy and related areas. The programmes listed for the 2027–2028 scholarship cycle are: 1. Master of Science in Global Technology and Development The MS in Global Technology and Development focuses on the relationship between technology, development and global challenges. The programme is particularly relevant to applicants interested in understanding how technological innovation can be applied to address development challenges and improve social and economic outcomes. Learn more about the MS Global Technology and Development programme 2. Master of Science in Information Technology The MS in Information Technology provides advanced study in information technology and related technical areas. It may be particularly relevant to applicants seeking careers involving information systems, technology management, digital transformation and other technology-related fields. Learn more about the MS Information Technology programme 3. Master of Science in Human Systems Engineering – Intelligent Systems This programme focuses on intelligent systems and the interaction between people and technological systems. It provides an option for applicants interested in areas involving human-centred technological systems, intelligent technologies and the design of systems that interact effectively with people. Learn more about the Human Systems Engineering – Intelligent Systems programme 4. Master of Science in Computer Science The MS in Computer Science provides graduate-level study in computing and computer science. It is suitable for applicants interested in developing advanced technical knowledge that can support careers and research in areas of computing and technology. Learn more about the Computer Science master s programme 5. Master of Science in Data Science, Analytics and Engineering The scholarship includes the Computing and Decision Analytics pathway within ASU s Data Science, Analytics and Engineering programme. This area is relevant to applicants interested in using data, computational methods and analytical approaches to address complex problems and support better decision-making. Learn more about the Data Science, Analytics and Engineering programme 6. Master of Science in Robotics and Autonomous Systems The MS in Robotics and Autonomous Systems provides advanced study related to robotics and autonomous technologies. It is particularly relevant to applicants interested in emerging technologies, intelligent machines, automation and technological systems capable of operating with varying degrees of autonomy. Learn more about the Robotics and Autonomous Systems programme 7. Master of Science in Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering This programme provides graduate-level study connected to civil engineering, environmental challenges and sustainability. It may be especially relevant to applicants interested in developing engineering solutions to infrastructure, environmental and sustainable-development challenges. Learn more about the Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering programme 8. Master of Science in Clean Energy Systems The MS in Clean Energy Systems focuses on technologies and systems associated with clean and sustainable energy. The programme is relevant to applicants who want to contribute to the transition toward more sustainable energy systems and address energy-related challenges. Learn more about the Clean Energy Systems programme 9. Master of Science in Modern Energy Production and Sustainable Use This programme focuses on modern approaches to energy production and sustainable energy use. It provides another pathway for applicants interested in energy innovation, sustainability and the development of more effective energy systems. Learn more about the Modern Energy Production and Sustainable Use programme What Does the Mastercard Foundation Scholarship Cover? One of the most significant features of this opportunity is the breadth of financial and academic support available to selected scholars. The scholarship covers several major expenses associated with studying in the United States. Full Tuition and Required Fees Selected scholars receive support toward full tuition and required student fees for the programme. This removes one of the largest financial barriers associated with pursuing a master s degree at a US university. Required Books The scholarship includes support for required books, helping scholars obtain the academic materials needed for their studies. On-Campus Housing Selected scholars receive on-campus accommodation . This is particularly important for international students relocating to Arizona because housing can represent a substantial part of the cost of studying in the United States. Medical Support The scholarship provides medical support/healthcare coverage as part of the comprehensive support package. Visa-Related Costs The scholarship covers visa application processing costs , helping reduce the financial burden associated with obtaining the necessary visa to study in the United States. Airfare The scholarship provides airfare to and from Phoenix, Arizona , supporting scholars with the international travel required to begin and complete their studies. English Language Test Support An English language proficiency test voucher may be provided if the applicant is required to take such a test. ASU Graduate Application Fee Waiver Applicants who are selected to advance to the stage where they are invited to apply for ASU admission will receive an ASU application fee waiver . Applicants should therefore not pay an ASU application fee if they have been invited to apply through the scholarship process and provided with the waiver. Leadership Development and Signature Programming The scholarship goes beyond traditional financial assistance. Scholars participate in leadership development and signature programming intended to strengthen their personal, professional and leadership capabilities. The ASU programme also identifies academic advising, support and leadership development among the elements of the scholarship experience. Internship and Practical Experience The current ASU programme information also identifies a two-month internship between the first and second years as part of the scholarship experience. This practical component can help scholars connect classroom learning with professional experience and develop skills that can be applied after graduation. Leadership, Mentorship and Community Engagement The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is structured around the idea that higher education should contribute to broader social transformation. As a result, scholars are expected to engage in leadership development, professional development and community-oriented activities. The ASU programme places emphasis on developing leaders who can use their education to contribute to economic growth and social development, particularly in Africa. The wider ASU Mastercard Foundation programme also highlights: Leadership development Professional development Community service Academic support Peer mentorship Transition support Career preparation Community engagement Giving back to communities Development of social ventures and impactful initiatives This means that applicants should not think of the scholarship purely as a financial award. The programme seeks candidates who have demonstrated a commitment to leadership and service and who can articulate how their education will contribute to positive change. Eligibility Requirements for the 2027 Scholarship Applicants must satisfy the programme s eligibility requirements before submitting an application. 1. Bachelor s Degree Requirement Applicants must have earned, or be on track to earn, a bachelor s degree by August 2027 from a recognised institution. The scholarship specifically states that higher education diplomas, certificates and other non-degree credentials are not considered equivalent to a bachelor s degree for this requirement. Applicants who do not hold a bachelor s degree should therefore not assume that another post-secondary qualification will satisfy the requirement. 2. Strong Academic Record Applicants must demonstrate a strong academic record equivalent to a minimum: 3.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate strong performance. Because international grading systems differ, applicants should carefully consider how their academic credentials correspond to the stated requirement and provide accurate academic documentation. 3. English Language Proficiency Applicants must satisfy Arizona State University s English language proficiency requirements for graduate admission . Applicants who are required to demonstrate English proficiency should therefore be prepared to provide the relevant evidence. The scholarship application also indicates that an English language proficiency test voucher may be available if testing is required. 4. African Citizenship Applicants must be citizens of an African country . This scholarship is specifically designed as part of ASU s Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program focused on young African leaders. The ASU programme describes the current Innovation and Technology scholarship as supporting young African professionals pursuing master s degrees in technology and innovation. 5. Age Requirement Applicants must be: 18 to 33 years old on or before September 27, 2026 , the scholarship application deadline. Applicants outside the stated age range should carefully review the official programme guidance before applying. 6. Leadership and Community Service Applicants must demonstrate a record of: Leadership Service Community engagement Commitment to creating positive change This is an important part of the scholarship because the programme is designed to develop future leaders who will use their education to contribute to their communities. Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate concrete examples rather than simply stating that they are leaders. Examples may include community projects, volunteer work, professional initiatives, entrepreneurship, social-impact activities, student leadership, advocacy or other forms of meaningful service. 7. No Previous Graduate or Master s Degree Applicants must not have previously enrolled in or completed a graduate or master s degree programme . This requirement is important for applicants who already hold postgraduate qualifications. Applicants with an existing master s degree should not assume that they are eligible simply because they meet the academic or professional requirements. 8. No Concurrent Graduate Degree Applicants must not be enrolled in, or begin, another graduate or master s degree programme while applying for this scholarship. 9. Ability to Relocate to Arizona Applicants must be able to relocate to Tempe, Arizona, USA , and reside on the ASU campus for the duration of the programme. Because this is a full-time, on-campus graduate opportunity, applicants should be prepared for an international relocation and the demands of studying in a different academic and cultural environment. Who Should Consider Applying? This scholarship is particularly relevant to young African professionals and graduates who want to build advanced expertise in technology, innovation, computing, engineering, data, robotics, sustainable energy or related areas. Potential applicants may include individuals with backgrounds or interests in areas such as: Computer science Information technology Data science Artificial intelligence Robotics Engineering Sustainable engineering Clean energy Energy systems Technology and development Intelligent systems Digital innovation Technology-enabled development Sustainable technology However, applicants should not select a programme solely because it is covered by the scholarship. They should ensure that their academic background, interests, career objectives and future plans align with the requirements of the particular master s programme. Women, Refugees, Displaced Persons and People with Disabilities The programme explicitly encourages women, refugees and displaced persons, and people with disabilities to apply. This is consistent with the broader emphasis of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program on expanding access to higher education and supporting talented young people who may face barriers to educational opportunity. Eligible applicants from these groups should therefore not be discouraged from applying because of their background. Application Deadline The application deadline for the 2027–2028 Innovation and Technology Scholarship is: Sunday, September 27, 2026, at 23:59 GMT. Applications submitted after the stated deadline will not be considered. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit. Technical problems, incomplete documents, internet connectivity issues or errors in application information can create unnecessary risks close to the deadline. Important: Apply for the Scholarship Before Applying to ASU One of the most important instructions in the application process is that applicants should first complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program scholarship application . Applicants should not independently apply for admission to Arizona State University or to one of the graduate degree programmes unless instructed to do so by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program team . This distinction is important. Being interested in an ASU master s programme does not mean that applicants should immediately submit a separate paid graduate admission application. According to the application guidance, candidates who advance in the scholarship selection process will be invited to an interview and will receive guidance concerning the ASU admission process. Applicants who are subsequently invited to apply for ASU admission will receive an application fee waiver and should not pay an application fee. Connect Technology to Social or Economic Impact The scholarship is specifically focused on innovation and technology. For example, applicants might discuss how technology can contribute to: Education Healthcare Agriculture Financial inclusion Energy access Climate resilience Public services Employment Entrepreneurship Infrastructure Digital transformation The strongest applications should show a connection between the applicant s academic interests, professional goals and broader community impact. Demonstrate Commitment to Africa The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ASU places significant emphasis on preparing scholars to contribute to economic and social development in Africa. What Happens After the Initial Application? Applicants should understand that submission is not necessarily the end of the selection process. Candidates who are selected to advance may be: Invited to an interview. Given further guidance regarding the ASU graduate admission process. title: Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027: Apply for $30,000 to Build Bold Social Justice Ideas
summary: The Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from social justice changemakers in the United States who have bold, early-stage ideas aimed at creating meaningful social change. The six-month fellowship provides selected fellows with a $30,000 award , a $1,000 healthcare stipend , coaching and mentorship, peer support, and fully funded travel to three in-person fellowship convenings. Unlike many traditional funding opportunities, the Voqal Partners Fellowship is specifically designed for people who are still developing an idea. Applicants do not need to have an established organization, completed product, fully developed campaign, or comprehensive business plan. Instead, Voqal Partners is interested in individuals who recognize a systemic problem, have a compelling vision for changing it, and are ready to begin testing, developing, and learning from their idea. Applications for the 2027 cohort close on October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time . Opportunity Overview Opportunity: Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 Category: Fellowship Fellowship duration: Six months Award: $30,000 Healthcare support: $1,000 healthcare stipend Additional support: Coaching, mentorship, peer learning and community Travel: Fully funded travel to three in-person convenings Childcare support: Available for fellows with dependents under 18 Location requirement: United States Project focus: Social justice and systemic change Application deadline: October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Fellowship period: April–September 2027 What Is the Voqal Partners Fellowship? The Voqal Partners Fellowship is a six-month program designed to support people who are developing ambitious ideas for social justice and systemic change. The fellowship recognizes that many potentially transformative ideas never receive funding because they are considered too early, too unconventional, or too difficult to fit into traditional philanthropic funding models. Voqal Partners takes a different approach by supporting people at the dream or idea stage and giving them the resources and environment they need to explore what their ideas could become. The program is therefore not necessarily looking for applicants with an established nonprofit organization or an already successful initiative. An applicant may still be determining the best structure for their project, testing assumptions, exploring a new approach, or figuring out how a promising idea could be implemented. The central question is whether the applicant has a strong vision for creating a more equitable future and a realistic starting point for exploring that vision. During the fellowship, selected fellows receive financial support, coaching, mentorship, peer learning opportunities, and access to a community of other changemakers. The program is intended to help fellows move their ideas from an early concept toward real-world experimentation. What Does the $30,000 Fellowship Award Cover? Each selected fellow receives a $30,000 award , generally distributed as a lump sum at the beginning of the fellowship. One of the distinctive features of the Voqal Partners Fellowship is the flexibility attached to the funding. Fellows are not restricted to spending the money only on narrowly defined project expenses. The funding can support expenses such as: Living expenses Equipment Contractors or additional assistance Travel Project implementation Research and experimentation Other costs that help the fellow develop their idea If a particular expense helps the fellow move their idea forward, it is generally considered an appropriate use of the fellowship funding. Voqal Partners can also work with fellows who prefer to receive their funding according to a particular schedule, such as through monthly payments. The organization indicates that the full award can be distributed according to an agreed timeline as long as the entire amount is provided by the end of the fellowship. This flexible funding structure allows fellows to determine what they need most during the six-month period rather than having every expense predetermined by the funder. $1,000 Healthcare Stipend In addition to the $30,000 fellowship award, selected fellows receive a $1,000 healthcare stipend . This additional support recognizes that personal wellbeing and health can affect a person s ability to pursue demanding social justice work. The stipend provides an additional financial resource for fellows during the fellowship period. Fully Funded Travel to Three Fellowship Convenings The fellowship includes three in-person convenings scheduled during the program. These gatherings are an important component of the fellowship because they provide opportunities for fellows to: Meet and learn from other fellows Participate in peer learning Work with coaches and advisors Develop relationships with members of the Voqal community Reflect on their work Collaborate around challenges and opportunities Strengthen their ideas through collective learning Voqal Partners covers the travel costs associated with these gatherings. Fellows with dependents under the age of 18 can also receive childcare support, helping reduce one of the practical barriers that can prevent caregivers from participating fully in professional development and fellowship programs. Coaching, Mentorship and Professional Support Financial support is only one part of the Voqal Partners Fellowship. Selected fellows gain access to coaches, advisors and mentors who can help them think through the challenges involved in turning an early-stage idea into something that can be tested in the real world. This support can include discussions around: Strategy Operations Organizational development Structural challenges Project development Experimentation Leadership Community engagement Future opportunities Because fellows may be working on ideas that challenge existing systems, the coaching component can provide an important opportunity to examine assumptions, identify obstacles and determine practical next steps. A Small Cohort of Social Justice Changemakers Voqal Partners selects only eight fellows each year . The small cohort model allows fellows to develop close relationships with one another and create a community around shared learning. Rather than going through the fellowship experience independently, participants learn alongside other people who are also attempting to develop ambitious ideas for social change. Past fellows remain connected through an active alumni network, creating opportunities for relationships and knowledge-sharing to continue after the formal six-month fellowship ends. Who Is Voqal Partners Looking For? The Voqal Partners Fellowship is aimed at people who are deeply connected to the communities and issues they are working to address. The organization emphasizes that applicants should not simply approach communities from the outside with solutions. Instead, it prioritizes people who are part of the communities they serve and who have a strong understanding of the challenges those communities face. Voqal Partners particularly values: Community leaders Organizers Builders Visionaries People with lived experience People developing unconventional approaches to social justice Individuals working alongside communities affected by systemic problems People seeking to support historically excluded communities The fellowship also encourages applications from individuals and communities that have traditionally had difficulty accessing philanthropic funding. These include, among others: LGBTQIA+ individuals Women Indigenous peoples People of color People with disabilities The emphasis is not simply on demographic identity. Voqal Partners also wants to understand an applicant s relationship with the community, their lived experience, their vision for change, and their ability to contribute meaningfully to the work. What Does Dream-Stage or Idea-Stage Mean? One of the most important aspects of the Voqal Partners Fellowship is its focus on dream-stage and idea-stage projects . This means applicants do not necessarily need to have everything figured out before applying. For example, an applicant might: Have identified a major social problem but still be determining the best solution. Have a new approach they want to test. Be exploring how a community-led initiative could work. Have an early concept for a campaign or project. Have an idea for disrupting an existing system. Be developing a new model for organizing or community participation. Need time and resources to determine whether an unconventional idea can work. The fellowship is designed to provide space for this kind of exploration. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that their idea is too early simply because they do not yet have a finished organization, product, campaign or business plan. What Types of Projects Does Voqal Partners Support? Voqal Partners seeks ideas that have the potential to challenge or disrupt systems rather than simply making existing systems easier to navigate. The organization is particularly interested in projects with a compelling vision for the future. Projects may be: Hyperlocal Community-based National in scope However, the work must focus on communities in the United States . The scale of the project is therefore less important than the quality of the vision, the relationship with the affected community, and the potential for the proposed work to contribute to meaningful systemic change. Key Qualities Voqal Partners Looks For Applicants should consider five major characteristics when assessing whether their project fits the fellowship. 1. Dream-stage or idea-stage work The idea may still be developing. Applicants do not need to present a finished initiative. What matters is having a bold vision and being ready to explore how that vision could become reality. 2. A compelling vision Voqal Partners is interested in ideas that challenge the status quo. The organization seeks approaches that can potentially disrupt systems through transformative solutions rather than simply creating small interventions that make existing systems more comfortable. 3. A path forward Having a big idea is not enough. Applicants should also demonstrate that they have some thoughts about where they could begin. This could include identifying: What they want to test What they want to learn What they want to build Which assumptions they need to explore What initial steps they could take during the fellowship The path does not need to be completely developed because the fellowship itself is intended to provide space for learning and experimentation. 4. Alignment with the fellowship Applicants should explain why the Voqal Partners Fellowship is appropriate for their idea. The application should demonstrate how the fellowship s funding, coaching, mentorship and community could help move the project forward. 5. Connection to community Applicants should be able to explain their relationship with the people most affected by the issue they are addressing. Voqal Partners places significant emphasis on community connection and the role an applicant plays in advancing the work. Fellowship Responsibilities The Voqal Partners Fellowship provides substantial freedom, but fellows are also expected to actively participate in the program. Fellows are expected to: Work on their fellowship project from April through September 2027. Attend three in-person convenings. Participate in monthly cohort calls. Engage with coaches and advisors. Share what they learned at the conclusion of the fellowship. The three convenings are scheduled for: April 2027: Opening convening July 2027: Middle convening September 2027: Closing convening Although fellows are permitted to pursue other employment or responsibilities during the fellowship, Voqal Partners asks them to make their fellowship project a priority. This flexibility may be particularly useful for applicants who have existing professional, family or community responsibilities. Do Fellows Keep Ownership of Their Ideas? Yes. Fellows retain full ownership of intellectual property developed during the fellowship. Voqal Partners does not claim ownership of a fellow s ideas, products or creations. This is an important consideration for applicants developing innovative concepts because it means the fellowship does not require fellows to surrender ownership of intellectual property created as part of their work. Can Previous Applicants Apply Again? Yes. Previous applicants are encouraged to apply again. Voqal Partners recognizes that strong ideas can evolve over time. Applying in a previous year does not prevent someone from submitting a new application or returning with an idea that has developed further. The organization also indicates that previous applications do not negatively affect future consideration. Can Previous Fellows Apply? The supplied fellowship information includes this question in the FAQ section, but does not provide a complete answer in the provided material. Applicants who have previously participated as fellows should therefore verify their eligibility directly with Voqal Partners before submitting an application. Can Fellows Have Other Jobs? Yes. Fellows are permitted to pursue other work during the fellowship. Voqal Partners recognizes that fellows may have employment, family obligations and other responsibilities. However, the organization expects the fellowship project to remain a priority throughout the program. This means applicants do not necessarily need to leave their existing employment to participate. Application Process The Voqal Partners Fellowship application is divided into four primary sections. Section 1: Eligibility The first part of the application contains questions designed to establish whether the applicant meets the fellowship s core eligibility requirements. Applicants should carefully review these requirements before investing significant time in the application. Section 2: Basic Details This section collects fundamental information about the applicant and their proposed project. Applicants may be asked for: Information about how they found the fellowship Their project name Brief project descriptions Basic personal details Section 3: The Specifics This is the central part of the application. Applicants will need to explain the future they are trying to create, how they envision moving toward that future, and what kind of support they would need from the fellowship. This section is likely to be particularly important because it gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate the strength of their vision and their connection to the issue they are addressing. Applicants should focus on clearly communicating: The problem they are addressing Why the problem matters Their vision for change What makes their approach different What they want to explore or test What they hope to learn Why they are well positioned to pursue the idea How Voqal Partners could help Section 4: Additional Details The final section provides space for additional information. Applicants may be asked about: Their use of artificial intelligence Previous experience with coaches Additional information relevant to their application Links Supporting documents Other details they believe the selection team should know The Fellowship Budget Applicants must also submit a budget explaining how they anticipate using the $30,000 fellowship award . Importantly, Voqal Partners states that the budget is not used to evaluate the application . Instead, the budget helps the organization understand where the applicant currently stands in their planning. A budget template is provided as part of the application. Applicants should therefore use the budget to provide a realistic picture of what they believe they will need rather than attempting to create an artificially sophisticated financial plan. Application Resources Applicants can prepare for the application using resources provided by Voqal Partners, including: The application guide The fellowship question list The online application Virtual information sessions Reviewing the application guide and question list before beginning the application can help applicants understand what information they will need and organize their responses in advance. Voqal Partners Fellowship Information Sessions Voqal Partners is offering two virtual information sessions for prospective applicants. The organization states that both sessions will cover the same information, meaning applicants only need to attend one. Session 1 Date: September 18, 2026 Time: 12:00 p.m. Eastern / 9:00 a.m. Pacific Format: Virtual The first session will be recorded, with the recording expected to be shared afterward. Session 2 Date: October 14, 2026 Time: 4:00 p.m. Eastern / 1:00 p.m. Pacific Format: Virtual Applicants who cannot attend the first session can participate in the second session. 2027 Fellowship Timeline Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Applications Open First Tuesday after Labor Day 2026 Applications Close October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Interviews January 2027 Fellows Selected February–March 2027 Opening Convening April 2027 Fellowship Programming April–September 2027 Middle Convening July 2027 Closing Convening September 2027 Because the application deadline is specific to a time zone, applicants should avoid waiting until the final day and should submit well before the stated closing time. How to Strengthen Your Voqal Partners Fellowship Application Although there is no guaranteed formula for selection, applicants can take several practical steps to make their application clearer and more compelling. Clearly explain the future you want to create Do not focus exclusively on describing what is wrong. Explain what the world, system or community could look like if your idea succeeds. Demonstrate your connection to the community Explain your relationship with the people affected by the issue. If you have lived experience, community organizing experience or another meaningful connection to the issue, make that relationship clear. Show why your idea is different Voqal Partners is interested in bold ideas that can challenge existing systems. Explain what makes your proposed approach different from conventional solutions. Be honest about what you do not know Because the fellowship is designed for early-stage ideas, applicants do not need to pretend that every detail has already been solved. Instead, identify the questions you need to answer and the assumptions you want to test. Explain what you would do with the fellowship Be specific about how the six months could help you move from an idea toward experimentation. Consider explaining: What you would investigate What you would build Who you would engage What you would test What resources you need What you hope to learn Prepare a realistic budget Even though the budget does not determine the evaluation of your application, it should demonstrate that you have thought carefully about how the fellowship resources could support your work. Use the application guide Review the official application guide and question list before submitting. This can help you understand the application structure and avoid overlooking important questions. Examples of Previous Fellows Work The fellowship has previously supported projects addressing civic participation, grassroots organizing and worker advocacy. Andrea Hart — City Bureau Andrea Hart worked on a civic newsroom model designed to train residents to report on local government and conduct community-driven investigations. The example illustrates how the fellowship can support approaches that strengthen community participation in civic life and local accountability. Erick Garcia — #GAMETHESYSTEM Erick Garcia developed a gamified approach to grassroots organizing, using digital tools to increase participation and accessibility. This demonstrates the type of experimentation that can emerge when technology and organizing are combined in unconventional ways. Rich Wallace — Equity Transformation Rich Wallace organized workers in the informal economy to pursue policy protections at city and state levels. The project demonstrates another dimension of the fellowship s focus: supporting efforts that seek structural and policy-level change for communities that may otherwise have limited access to institutional power. Why the Voqal Partners Fellowship Is Different The fellowship stands out because of its willingness to fund ideas before they have become fully established projects. Traditional funding opportunities frequently require applicants to demonstrate previous results, organizational infrastructure, detailed implementation plans or established programs. The Voqal Partners model is more focused on the person, their vision and the possibility of what their idea could become. Its approach combines: Flexible funding Personal financial support Healthcare assistance Coaching Mentorship Peer learning Community Fully funded travel Continued alumni engagement The result is an opportunity for social justice changemakers to dedicate meaningful time and resources to exploring an idea that may otherwise struggle to receive conventional funding. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for social justice changemakers who meet the organization s eligibility requirements and have a bold vision for creating a more equitable future. Applicants must: Be 18 years of age or older . Be based in the United States . Be able to receive funds in the United States . Be working on an idea connected to communities in the United States. Have a social justice-oriented vision or idea. Be prepared to dedicate the fellowship period to developing and testing the idea. Be willing and able to participate in the fellowship s required activities, including the three in-person convenings. Voqal Partners does not provide visa sponsorship. The organization particularly encourages applications from people with lived experience and individuals connected to communities historically excluded from philanthropy. APPLY HERE Geographic Eligibility This is not a worldwide fellowship . The fellowship requires applicants to be based in the United States and able to receive funds in the United States . Projects may be local, regional or national in scope, but the work must focus on communities within the United States. Therefore, applicants living in countries outside the United States, including applicants from African countries such as Kenya, do not meet the stated geographic eligibility requirement unless they independently satisfy Voqal Partners U.S.-based eligibility requirements. Important Deadline The application deadline for the Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 is October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time . Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their application. Technical problems, incomplete responses or missing documents can create unnecessary difficulties close to the deadline. A good strategy is to complete the application ahead of time, review every response, check the budget and submit before the final day. How to Apply Interested applicants should use the official Voqal Partners application portal to begin their application. Before applying, prospective fellows should also review the official application guide and question list so they understand what is expected. Applicants who have questions can contact Voqal Partners through fellowship@voqalpartners.org . Visit HERE to learn more about the Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027. Frequently Asked Questions Is the Voqal Partners Fellowship fully funded? The fellowship provides a $30,000 award, a $1,000 healthcare stipend and covers travel costs associated with the three required in-person convenings. Childcare support is also available for fellows with dependents under 18. Do I need an established organization to apply? No. The fellowship specifically welcomes dream-stage and idea-stage work. Applicants do not need a finished organization, product, campaign or business plan. Can I use the $30,000 for living expenses? Yes. The funding has no stated restrictions on how fellows use the award, provided the expenses support the fellow and their work. This can include living expenses, equipment, contractors, travel and implementation costs. Do I keep ownership of my intellectual property? Yes. Fellows retain ownership of intellectual property developed during the fellowship. Can I work another job during the fellowship? Yes. Other work is permitted, although fellows are expected to prioritize their fellowship project. How many fellows are selected? Voqal Partners selects eight fellows each year . Are previous applicants allowed to apply? Yes. Previous applicants are encouraged to apply again. Does Voqal Partners sponsor visas? No. The organization does not offer visa sponsorship. Must I attend the in-person convenings? Yes. Attendance at all three convenings is a core part of the fellowship experience. What happens to my application information? Voqal Partners states that applications are reviewed by a select group of community members, including program alumni, staff and partners. Access is limited to the evaluation period, and the organization states that it will not share applicants ideas or details beyond this process without their knowledge. Conclusion The Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 offers a distinctive opportunity for social justice changemakers who have ambitious ideas but may not yet have the organizational infrastructure, funding or resources needed to turn those ideas into reality. With $30,000 in flexible funding , a $1,000 healthcare stipend , coaching and mentorship, peer support, fully funded travel to three convenings and access to an alumni community, the fellowship is designed to give selected changemakers the time and resources to explore, test and develop new approaches to systemic change. The opportunity is particularly relevant to people with lived experience and strong connections to the communities they serve, especially individuals from groups historically excluded from traditional philanthropy. However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the geographic requirement. The fellowship is U.S.-based , applicants must be 18 or older, based in the United States and able to receive funds in the U.S. , and Voqal Partners does not provide visa sponsorship. For eligible applicants with a bold social justice idea, the October 31, 2026 deadline provides an important opportunity to seek support for an idea that may be too early or unconventional for traditional funding programs. Applicants should begin by reviewing the application guide and question list, developing a clear explanation of the future they want to create, identifying what they want to test or learn during the six-month fellowship, and preparing a realistic budget for the $30,000 award.
