title: British Academy Elevate Programme Leadership Stream: Apply for an Intensive Leadership Development Programme for Early Career Researchers
summary: The British Academy Elevate Programme – Leadership Stream is an intensive, CPD-accredited professional development programme designed to help Early Career Researchers (ECRs) develop the leadership skills, confidence, networks and practical experience needed to progress in academia and beyond. Delivered by the British Academy , the UK’s national academy for the humanities and social sciences, the Elevate Programme combines structured leadership training with mentoring, coaching, networking and practical opportunities to apply newly acquired skills. The programme is particularly suited to Early Career Researchers in SHAPE disciplines who are preparing to take on leadership responsibilities or are already moving into leadership positions. The programme is highly selective, with approximately 62 participants selected each year from the British Academy Early Career Researcher Network and Wellcome-funded researchers. The annual programme normally runs from March to June , while applications open in September . Participants take part in a combination of online and in-person activities, depending on where they are based. What Is the British Academy Elevate Programme – Leadership Stream? The British Academy Elevate Programme—Leadership Stream is a structured leadership development initiative created specifically for Early Career Researchers. Rather than focusing exclusively on academic research skills, the programme addresses the broader professional capabilities researchers need to become effective leaders. These include communication, strategic planning, research management, collaboration, influencing decision-making, and managing teams and projects. The programme recognises that leadership opportunities can arise at different stages of an academic or research career. As a result, it is designed to be adaptable to researchers at early, mid and later stages of their early-career journey. Participants are supported through a combination of: Leadership training Interactive workshops Professional mentoring Individual and group coaching Peer networking Practical leadership activities Opportunities to apply leadership skills in professional settings Post-programme engagement with the wider Early Career Researcher Network The programme therefore provides participants with both theoretical understanding and practical experience that can be applied directly to their research, academic, professional or organisational responsibilities. Key Features of the British Academy Elevate Leadership Programme The Elevate Programme is designed around several interconnected elements of professional development. 1. Intensive leadership training Participants receive structured training focused on developing the skills required to become effective leaders. The training can help researchers understand how to: Lead projects effectively Manage teams and responsibilities Communicate with different audiences Influence decision-making Develop strategic approaches to their work Navigate professional challenges Build productive collaborations Manage research-related activities Drive positive change within organisations and institutions The emphasis is on practical leadership rather than leadership theory alone. 2. Interactive workshops The programme includes interactive workshops that allow participants to explore leadership concepts and apply them to real professional situations. These workshops provide opportunities for participants to learn from facilitators and fellow researchers while considering how leadership principles can be used in their own careers. The interactive format can also help participants develop confidence in areas such as communication, teamwork, problem-solving and strategic thinking. 3. Mentoring Mentoring forms an important component of the programme. Through mentoring, participants can benefit from guidance, experience and perspectives that can help them navigate their career development and leadership responsibilities. Mentoring can be particularly valuable for Early Career Researchers who are preparing to transition into positions where they need to coordinate people, manage projects, influence stakeholders or take greater responsibility for research and organisational outcomes. 4. Coaching Participants also receive coaching as part of the programme. Coaching provides an opportunity to reflect on individual leadership strengths, challenges and development areas. It can help researchers identify practical approaches for becoming more effective in their professional roles. This combination of training, mentoring and coaching gives participants multiple forms of support throughout the programme. 5. Peer networking The programme brings together a selective group of Early Career Researchers, creating opportunities for participants to develop professional relationships with peers. Networking can enable participants to: Exchange ideas and experiences Learn from researchers working in different areas Develop professional connections Identify potential collaborators Share approaches to common leadership challenges Build relationships that can continue beyond the programme The peer network is an important part of the wider professional development experience offered by Elevate. What Skills Will Participants Develop? The British Academy Elevate Programme is designed to develop a broad range of leadership and professional competencies. Participants will have the opportunity to strengthen their ability to: Lead projects and initiatives Researchers often become responsible for projects involving multiple people, institutions or stakeholders. The programme helps participants develop the leadership capabilities required to coordinate such activities effectively. Manage teams Effective leadership requires more than technical expertise. Researchers stepping into leadership roles may need to delegate responsibilities, support colleagues, manage expectations and foster productive working relationships. The programme provides training relevant to these responsibilities. Communicate effectively Communication is a central component of leadership. Participants develop practical knowledge that can help them communicate ideas, expectations, strategies and decisions more effectively. Influence decision-making Researchers increasingly need to communicate their evidence and expertise to decision-makers both inside and outside academia. The Elevate Programme helps participants build confidence and skills for influencing decisions and engaging with different stakeholders. Develop strategic thinking Strategic planning is another important component of effective leadership. Participants gain practical knowledge that can help them think beyond individual tasks and consider broader objectives, priorities, resources and long-term outcomes. Manage research effectively The programme also supports researchers in developing skills related to research management. This can be particularly valuable for researchers who are beginning to coordinate larger projects, work with teams or take responsibility for complex research activities. Navigate professional challenges Leadership often involves dealing with uncertainty, competing priorities, difficult decisions and unexpected challenges. Through training, coaching and peer learning, participants can develop greater confidence in navigating these situations. Foster collaboration Modern research frequently depends on collaboration across disciplines, organisations and professional networks. The programme supports participants in developing collaborative approaches and building relationships that can contribute to stronger professional and research outcomes. Who Can Benefit From the Programme? The British Academy Elevate Leadership Stream is designed for Early Career Researchers, particularly those working in SHAPE disciplines . SHAPE refers broadly to disciplines within the social sciences, humanities and related areas, covering fields where researchers study people, societies, cultures, economies, institutions and human behaviour. The programme can be relevant to researchers who are: Preparing to move into leadership roles Already taking on leadership responsibilities Managing or contributing to research projects Interested in developing their professional leadership capabilities Seeking to strengthen their communication and strategic planning skills Interested in research management Looking to expand their professional networks Considering leadership opportunities within or beyond academia Importantly, the programme is adaptable to different stages of the early-career journey. A Programme Designed for Leadership Inside and Outside Academia One of the strengths of the Elevate Leadership Stream is that its benefits are not restricted to traditional academic career pathways. The leadership skills developed through the programme can potentially be applied in areas such as: Academic leadership Research management Policy engagement Organisational leadership Professional services Public engagement Research funding and stakeholder engagement Mentoring and skills development Leadership positions outside academia This broader focus makes the programme relevant to researchers who want to translate their research and professional expertise into wider societal and organisational impact. Delivery Format of the British Academy Elevate Programme The programme uses a combination of online and face-to-face learning. Participants can expect a mixture of: Online workshops In-person workshops Specialised training sessions Mentoring Coaching Networking events Practical post-programme activities In-person participation for UK-based researchers Researchers based in the UK should be prepared for approximately 10 in-person training sessions . Each in-person session lasts approximately one to two days and takes place at a different location in the UK. Consequently, UK-based participants should be prepared to travel to the various locations where the training sessions are held. Within nine months of completing the programme , participants are required to organise an event or activity for the Early Career Researcher Network. For participants, CPD accreditation adds professional recognition to the leadership training received through the programme. This can be valuable when demonstrating professional development to: Employers Research institutions Academic institutions Funders Professional organisations Potential collaborators The accreditation can also strengthen a participant s professional profile by providing evidence of structured leadership development. GetTWOit Skills Passport and Micro-Credentials Participants in the British Academy Elevate Programme can also receive a GetTWOit Skills Passport documenting the skills acquired through the programme. A Skills Passport is provided for each completed training session, creating a structured record of the professional skills developed. This can help participants demonstrate specific competencies rather than simply stating that they attended a leadership programme. The Skills Passport functions as a form of micro-credential and can provide additional evidence of professional learning. Skills Passport after the Network event Participants can also receive a GetTWOit Skills Passport after organising an event for the Early Career Researcher Network. This additional credential can demonstrate the participant s ability to take the leadership training they received and use it to develop or deliver learning activities for other Early Career Researchers. It therefore provides evidence not only of participation in training but also of practical leadership and knowledge-sharing. How the Programme Can Strengthen Your CV Professional development programmes can be particularly useful for researchers who are building their academic or professional profiles. The British Academy Elevate Programme offers several elements that can contribute to a stronger CV. Participants can potentially demonstrate: Completion of CPD-accredited leadership training Leadership development Project management capabilities Team management skills Strategic planning experience Communication skills Research management experience Networking and collaboration Mentoring experience Event or activity organisation Peer-to-peer knowledge sharing Practical application of leadership skills The programme is therefore structured to provide tangible evidence of professional development that can be communicated to employers and funders. Why Leadership Skills Matter for Early Career Researchers Research careers increasingly require researchers to operate beyond the boundaries of individual research projects. As researchers progress, they may be expected to manage teams, coordinate projects, communicate findings to different audiences, collaborate across institutions, secure funding, engage policymakers or contribute to organisational strategy. Technical research expertise remains essential, but leadership and interpersonal skills can also play a significant role in career progression. The Elevate Programme addresses this broader professional development need by combining research-sector knowledge with leadership development. Networking and Long-Term Professional Development Another important aspect of the programme is the opportunity to become part of a community of Early Career Researchers. These connections can potentially support: Future research collaborations Knowledge exchange Professional mentoring Cross-disciplinary relationships Career advice Leadership development Peer learning Engagement with the wider research community The requirement to mentor a subsequent cohort further strengthens the programme s emphasis on creating a continuing professional network rather than a one-time training experience. Their current or anticipated leadership responsibilities. The leadership skills they want to develop. How the programme fits into their career development. How they expect to apply the skills gained through Elevate. Their interest in collaboration and peer learning. Their ability to participate fully in the programme. title: WFP Ethics Officer P-3 in Rome, Italy: International Professional Job in Ethics, Compliance and Risk Management
summary: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is inviting applications for an Ethics Officer – P-3 position based at its headquarters in Rome, Italy . This is a full-time International Professional opportunity for an experienced ethics, compliance, legal, risk management or international affairs professional seeking to contribute to ethical governance and accountability within one of the world s largest humanitarian organizations. The position is located in the WFP Ethics Office and reports to the Senior Ethics Officer . The successful candidate will help strengthen WFP s ethical framework by advising employees and management, supporting conflict-of-interest disclosure processes, contributing to ethics-related policies, supporting protection against retaliation, developing training programmes, and strengthening relationships across WFP and the wider United Nations system. The application deadline is 29 September 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time (Rome) . WFP Ethics Officer P-3 Job at a Glance Opportunity Details Job title Ethics Officer – P-3 Organization World Food Programme (WFP) Job type International Professional Grade P-3 Job requisition JR126545 Location Rome, Italy Work arrangement Fully present/on-site Working hours Full time Contract Fixed-term, with a one-year probationary period Application deadline 29 September 2026, 23:59 CET Nationality Open to candidates of all nationalities Education Advanced university degree in a relevant field Experience At least 5 years of relevant progressively responsible experience Languages English at C level plus intermediate knowledge of a second official UN language Application documents CV and cover letter at the application stage WFP s official careers information describes P-3 positions as professional roles involving specialized and analytical responsibilities, with the complexity of responsibilities increasing with grade. International Professional positions generally operate under internationally determined compensation and benefits arrangements. About the World Food Programme The World Food Programme is the world s largest humanitarian organization. Its work focuses on saving lives during emergencies while using food assistance to support pathways toward peace, stability and prosperity for people affected by conflict, disasters and climate-related impacts. WFP operates through a large international workforce and a network of country, regional and headquarters offices. Its careers framework emphasizes meaningful work, continuous professional development and a multicultural working environment. WFP also places strong emphasis on integrity, collaboration, commitment, humanity and inclusion. These values are particularly relevant to an Ethics Officer because the position contributes directly to maintaining trust, accountability and responsible conduct across the organization. What Is the WFP Ethics Office? The Ethics Office plays an important role in helping WFP maintain high standards of integrity and ethical conduct. According to WFP, the Ethics Office is an independent and formal office that assists the Executive Director in nurturing a culture of ethics throughout the organization. It helps employees think through ethical dilemmas, understand relevant rules and policies, and raise concerns without fear of retaliation. The office s work includes several interconnected areas: Ethics advice and guidance Training, education and outreach Protection against retaliation Conflicts of interest and financial disclosures Ethical standards in policies and organizational practices Anti-fraud and anti-corruption principles Confidentiality and data protection considerations United Nations ethics coordination Support for ethical decision-making The WFP Code of Conduct reflects principles including human rights, social justice, dignity, equal rights, competence, integrity, impartiality and discretion. It also addresses areas such as anti-fraud and anti-corruption and protection against sexual exploitation and abuse. About the Ethics Officer – P-3 Position The Ethics Officer will work within the Ethics Office at WFP headquarters in Rome and report to the Senior Ethics Officer . The central purpose of the position is to support the development and maintenance of a robust ethical framework within WFP. This means the role is not limited to reviewing rules or responding to individual questions. It combines ethics advisory work, policy analysis, conflict-of-interest management, retaliation protection, training, communication, reporting and stakeholder engagement . The role therefore requires someone who can combine technical knowledge with strong interpersonal skills, discretion, independence and the ability to communicate sensitive issues clearly. Key Responsibilities of the Ethics Officer 1. Support the Ethics Office Strategy and Work Plan The Ethics Officer will provide substantive input into the definition and implementation of the Ethics Office s strategy and work plan. This involves helping determine priorities, activities and approaches that strengthen ethical standards across WFP. The role therefore requires an understanding of how ethics functions can be translated into practical organizational systems rather than treated simply as theoretical principles. 2. Provide Ethics Advice and Guidance A major part of the position involves providing timely advice and guidance to WFP employees and management on ethics and standards of conduct. The officer will also be responsible for properly tracking and recording ethics-related queries. This requires the ability to: Understand complex ethical situations Identify relevant policies and standards Provide clear and balanced advice Maintain confidentiality Exercise independent judgment Communicate effectively with different stakeholders Document advice and follow-up appropriately The importance of this function is reflected in the broader work of WFP s Ethics Office. Its 2025 annual report recorded 890 requests for ethics advice and guidance , with 96 percent of respondents to voluntary satisfaction surveys reporting that they were satisfied or very satisfied with the advice received and its timeliness. 3. Support the Annual Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure Programme The Ethics Officer will contribute to the management of WFP s annual disclosure programme. This includes reviewing disclosed conflicts of interest, providing advice and helping ensure the programme operates smoothly. Conflict-of-interest management is an important part of organizational integrity because employees may sometimes have private interests or outside activities that could conflict with their official responsibilities. WFP s Ethics Office explains that its annual disclosure programme is designed to identify and address such conflicts through disclosures involving assets, liabilities, investments and outside activities for certain categories of employees. For the Ethics Officer, this means applying ethical judgment to real situations and helping employees and management understand how potential conflicts should be identified and addressed. 4. Develop Ethics Training and Learning Programmes The successful candidate will help develop and deliver: Ethics training programmes E-learning modules Train-the-trainer programmes Sessions on WFP values Training on ethical principles Training on standards of conduct This responsibility requires more than technical knowledge. The Ethics Officer must also be able to explain complex concepts to employees with different professional and cultural backgrounds. WFP emphasizes training and outreach as important components of building an ethical culture because employees need to understand the values, standards and principles expected of them. 5. Advise on Ethics-Related Policies and Regulations The Ethics Officer will provide advice and review when WFP develops or updates: Policies Circulars Regulations Other organizational documents involving ethical considerations The officer may also be requested by other departments to provide ethics advice during policy development. This makes policy analysis an important component of the role. The successful candidate must therefore be comfortable reading complex institutional documents, identifying ethical implications and communicating recommendations clearly. 6. Support Protection Against Retaliation Another major responsibility involves supporting the review of requests for protection against retaliation. The officer may contribute to: Reviewing retaliation-protection requests Preparing memoranda Drafting responses to complainants Assessing relevant circumstances Applying whistleblower protection policies Maintaining confidentiality Supporting individuals who raise concerns WFP states that its Whistleblower Protection Policy is designed to protect employees from retaliation when they engage in protected activities, and that the protection applies to current and former employees regardless of contract type or duration. This is a particularly sensitive area of the position and requires independence, impartiality, careful listening and sound judgment. 7. Strengthen the Visibility of the Ethics Office The Ethics Officer will also contribute to enhancing the presence of the Ethics Office through: WFP internal websites External websites Online communication channels Relevant publications Other communication platforms This responsibility shows that the role also has a communication component. Ethics policies are most effective when employees understand them and know where to seek advice. Therefore, communicating the work of the Ethics Office clearly is part of strengthening an organization s ethical culture. 8. Support Reporting and Analysis The position will involve preparing analysis, drafting material and supporting reporting on the overall work of the Ethics Office. The officer may therefore need to translate complex information into: Reports Briefings Memos Analytical documents Policy notes Communication materials Strong analytical and writing abilities are consequently important. 9. Build Internal and External Relationships The Ethics Officer will build positive and effective relationships both within WFP and outside the organization. External cooperation may include engagement across: The United Nations system Other UN entities Rome-based UN agencies Professional ethics networks Relevant institutional partners WFP s Ethics Office already works to promote coherence across the United Nations system, including through cooperation with other ethics offices and Rome-based agencies. The successful candidate will therefore need strong interpersonal and partnership-building abilities. 10. Perform Other Duties as Assigned The officer may also undertake other responsibilities assigned by the Senior Ethics Officer when necessary to support the mandate of the Ethics Office and strengthen ethics and accountability across WFP. Minimum Education Requirements Applicants must have an advanced university degree in one of the following areas or a closely related discipline: Law Ethics Public administration International affairs Compliance Another related field This educational requirement makes the position particularly relevant to professionals with postgraduate qualifications in legal, governance, ethics, international policy or compliance-related disciplines. An advanced degree is important because the position requires the ability to interpret policies and regulations, assess ethical risks, advise senior stakeholders and prepare sophisticated written analysis. Professional Experience Required Candidates must have at least five years of relevant progressively responsible professional experience . The experience should be connected to areas such as: Legal advice Compliance Risk assessment Ethics Related professional fields The phrase progressively responsible is important. The position is not intended primarily for someone who has only completed an academic programme or gained limited entry-level experience. Candidates should be able to demonstrate increasing responsibility and professional judgment in their previous roles. Relevant experience could involve advising organizations, reviewing compliance risks, developing policies, supporting investigations or whistleblower systems, providing ethics guidance, drafting legal or policy documents, or managing institutional risk. Knowledge and Skills Required The position requires a combination of technical, analytical and interpersonal skills. Understanding of Ethics, Compliance and Risk Candidates should have a theoretical understanding of: Ethics Compliance Risk assessment Standards of conduct Ethical decision-making The successful candidate must be able to apply this knowledge to practical organizational situations. Advisory Skills The Ethics Officer will advise a wide range of stakeholders on different ethical issues. This means applicants should be comfortable communicating with people at different levels of an international organization. Whistleblower Protection Knowledge Candidates must have technical knowledge of whistleblower protection policies. They should also demonstrate the ability to prepare: Legal memoranda Notes to file Analytical documents Written responses This is particularly relevant to the retaliation-protection component of the position. Independence and Impartiality Because the Ethics Office performs an independent and confidential function, the Ethics Officer must act with: Integrity Independence Impartiality Professional discretion The successful candidate must be able to provide objective advice even when dealing with sensitive or difficult situations. Interpersonal Skills WFP works with people from diverse professional, national and cultural backgrounds. The Ethics Officer must therefore be able to establish respectful working relationships and communicate effectively with colleagues from different backgrounds. Training and Facilitation Skills Applicants should demonstrate the ability to deliver training to small and medium-sized audiences. This is important because the role includes developing and facilitating ethics learning programmes. Active Listening The position specifically requires the ability to listen attentively to people seeking advice or protection from retaliation. This is particularly important because ethics-related cases may involve sensitive professional circumstances. Language Requirements The position requires: English: Fluency at Level C . In addition, candidates need intermediate knowledge at Level B of a second official United Nations language . The listed languages include: Arabic Chinese French Russian Spanish Portuguese This language requirement is particularly relevant to the international nature of the role. Candidates should therefore carefully assess their language proficiency before applying. Who Can Apply? The position is classified as an International Professional role and is open to candidates of all nationalities . This is an important distinction because the position is not restricted to Italian citizens or citizens of a particular region. Qualified professionals can therefore come from any country or continent, provided they meet the professional, academic and language requirements. WFP also explicitly states that it is committed to equal employment opportunity and encourages qualified candidates to apply regardless of: Race Colour National origin Ethnic background Social background Genetic information Gender Gender identity or expression Sexual orientation Religion or belief HIV status Disability Therefore, there is no race or ethnicity restriction attached to the position. However, being eligible to apply does not mean that an applicant will automatically be selected. Candidates must still meet the position s education, experience, skills and language requirements and successfully complete WFP s recruitment process. Location: Rome, Italy The position is based at WFP headquarters in Rome, Italy , within the Ethics Office. The vacancy is classified as fully present , meaning the selected candidate is expected to work from the designated workplace rather than remotely. The selected candidate will be required to relocate to Rome to take up the assignment. This is therefore an important consideration for candidates currently living outside Italy. Contract and International Professional Status The position is a fixed-term International Professional appointment with a one-year probationary period . The position is classified as non-rotational . This means that, under the conditions stated in the vacancy announcement, the incumbent is not subject to WFP s regular reassignment process unless the position is later reclassified as rotational. WFP explains that International Professional positions generally involve specialized and analytical work, with compensation and benefits determined according to applicable international civil service arrangements. Salary and Benefits The vacancy announcement describes an attractive compensation and benefits package in line with International Civil Service Commission standards. The listed benefits include: Basic salary Post adjustment Relocation entitlement Visa support Travel allowances Shipment allowances 30 days of annual leave Home leave Education grant for dependent children Pension plan Medical insurance These benefits are particularly relevant to international candidates who may need to relocate to Italy for the assignment. Applicants should note that the precise compensation package depends on the applicable terms and conditions of the appointment. Why Work for WFP? WFP presents several reasons why professionals may want to build their careers with the organization. Meaningful humanitarian work WFP s work directly supports people affected by emergencies, conflict, disasters and climate-related challenges. International working environment WFP operates with a highly multicultural workforce, creating opportunities to work alongside professionals from different countries and backgrounds. Professional development WFP invests in employee development through training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship and internal mobility opportunities. International career opportunities A career with WFP can potentially provide opportunities to work across country, regional and global offices. Nobel Peace Prize recognition WFP was awarded the 2020 Nobel Peace Prize , recognizing its contribution to efforts to prevent the use of hunger as a weapon of war and to peacebuilding efforts in conflict-affected areas. Why the Ethics Officer Role Matters to WFP Ethics may sometimes be viewed as an administrative function, but within a large humanitarian organization, it is closely connected to institutional credibility and operational effectiveness. WFP works in complex environments and handles significant responsibilities involving humanitarian assistance, partnerships, resources and people. Maintaining public and internal trust therefore requires strong standards of conduct and accountability. WFP s 2025 Ethics Office annual report notes that the organization operates in high-risk environments with a diverse and evolving workforce across more than 120 countries and territories. The report emphasizes the importance of safeguarding WFP s reputation and credibility and describes the Ethics Office as playing a vital role in providing timely guidance and supporting risk management. The Ethics Officer therefore contributes to an important institutional function: helping employees make sound ethical decisions and helping WFP maintain confidence in its operations. Examples of Ethics Work at WFP The broader work of the Ethics Office provides useful context for understanding this position. Ethics advice and guidance Employees can seek confidential advice when facing ethical questions or risks. Conflict-of-interest management The Ethics Office helps identify and address potential conflicts between private interests and official duties. Protection from retaliation The office supports mechanisms designed to protect employees who raise concerns about misconduct or wrongdoing. Training and awareness The Ethics Office conducts training and outreach to help employees understand expected standards. Policy and standards The office contributes to incorporating ethical considerations into organizational policies and practices. United Nations coherence The office works with other UN ethics bodies and Rome-based agencies to promote greater consistency and exchange of good practices. These functions closely correspond to the responsibilities outlined for the Ethics Officer position. Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications because the vacancy requires completion through WFP s online recruitment system. Apply for the WFP Ethics Officer – P-3 position At the application stage, the required documents are: CV Cover letter Additional documentation, such as a passport, certificates or recommendation letters, may be requested later in the recruitment process. Tailor your CV Your CV should clearly demonstrate relevant professional experience rather than simply listing every position you have held. Emphasize experience involving: Ethics Legal advisory work Compliance Risk assessment Whistleblower protection Policy development Governance Organizational accountability Training Investigations or related advisory functions International organizations Public administration 2. Demonstrate progressively responsible experience The vacancy requires five years of relevant progressively responsible experience. Applicants should show how their responsibilities have developed over time. For example, demonstrate progression from analytical or advisory responsibilities to roles involving greater independence, stakeholder engagement, policy responsibility or organizational decision-making. 3. Show policy-writing ability The role involves reviewing policies, circulars and regulations. Demonstrate training experience If you have delivered professional training, workshops, seminars or awareness sessions, highlight this clearly. Demonstrate interpersonal judgment The Ethics Officer will interact with people seeking advice and potentially individuals raising sensitive concerns. Clearly demonstrate language skills Because the position requires English at Level C and intermediate knowledge of another official UN language, applicants should accurately present their language abilities. Explain your interest in WFP A strong cover letter should demonstrate an understanding of WFP s humanitarian mission and explain why your professional background makes you suitable for contributing to its Ethics Office. title: Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development 2027 at AUC: Graduate Diploma Tuition Funding in Public Policy and Public Administration
summary: The American University in Cairo is inviting eligible graduate applicants to consider the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development, commonly abbreviated as SFID. Designed for academically strong students, the opportunity provides substantial tuition and fee support for graduate-diploma study in public policy or public administration at AUC. The credits completed through either diploma can also count toward the university’s Master of Public Policy or Master of Public Administration degree. This makes the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at AUC particularly relevant to applicants who want advanced training in public policy, governance, public administration, institutional development, or related public-service fields. In addition to academic study, recipients undertake a structured weekly work commitment with AUC’s Public Policy HUB, connecting their coursework with policy research and practical engagement. The fellowship is not open to every international applicant. AUC limits eligibility to Egyptian nationals and certain refugees residing in Egypt. Applicants must also meet the university’s graduate admission requirements and demonstrate an excellent academic record. Prospective candidates should therefore check both their nationality or refugee eligibility and their academic readiness before beginning the two-part application process. Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at a Glance Detail Information Host institution The American University in Cairo, Egypt Official name Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development (SFID) Supported study Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration Future academic pathway Diploma credits can count toward an MPP or MPA at AUC Duration Two semesters, subject to a satisfactory review after the first semester Tuition coverage Up to nine credits per semester Additional covered fees Student services and activities fees; medical service and health insurance fees Study status Full-time enrollment is required Academic standard while funded Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.2 Practical commitment At least 12 working hours each week with the Public Policy HUB Next application deadline November 2, 2026, for the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle Official information AUC Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development page What Is the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development? The Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development is an AUC graduate funding opportunity for new students with excellent academic performance. Its central purpose is to cover the credit hours required for an eligible graduate diploma in public policy or public administration. AUC explains that the same credits can subsequently count toward the Master of Public Policy or Master of Public Administration, allowing the diploma to function as a meaningful step toward a related master’s degree rather than as an isolated short course. The structure combines three important elements: Graduate-level academic training: Recipients enroll full-time in one of the two approved graduate-diploma programs. Financial support: The award covers tuition for a maximum of nine credits per semester and several mandatory university and health-related fees. Applied policy experience: Fellows contribute at least 12 working hours per week to AUC’s Public Policy HUB. The Public Policy HUB was created within AUC’s School of Global Affairs and Public Policy to help develop, test, refine, and communicate responses to public-policy challenges. It brings policy scholars and mentors together with emerging policy analysts and supports the production of policy research and briefs. Consequently, the weekly work requirement is a substantive part of the experience rather than a purely administrative condition. It can expose fellows to the process of turning policy ideas into structured analysis intended for policymakers and the wider public. More information about this initiative is available on the official Public Policy HUB page . Eligible Graduate Programs and Degree Pathways The fellowship is tied specifically to full-time study in one of the following AUC programs: Graduate Diploma in Public Policy Graduate Diploma in Public Administration Applicants should not assume that the award can be transferred to an unrelated graduate program. The official fellowship terms identify only these two diploma routes. An important feature is the relationship between the diplomas and AUC’s related master’s degrees. Credits earned while completing the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy can count toward the Master of Public Policy, while credits from the Graduate Diploma in Public Administration can count toward the Master of Public Administration. This arrangement may benefit candidates who want to build graduate credentials progressively, beginning with a diploma and later continuing toward a master’s degree. However, fellowship coverage is limited to the stated two-semester award and the eligible diploma credit hours. The fact that credits can count toward a later master’s degree does not mean that the fellowship automatically finances the remainder of an MPP or MPA. Applicants planning to continue should separately investigate the academic transition requirements, remaining degree credits, future tuition, and any other funding opportunities. Financial Coverage and Benefits AUC lists the following costs as covered by the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development: Tuition fees for up to nine credits per semester. Across the stated two-semester duration, this represents coverage of as many as 18 credits in total, provided the recipient remains eligible after the first-semester review. Student services and activities fees. These are university fees connected with the services and activities available to enrolled students. Medical service and health insurance fees. The award covers the health-related fees specifically named in the official terms. The phrase “full coverage” on the AUC fellowship page refers to the credit hours needed to complete the eligible graduate diploma, within the maximum of nine funded credits per semester. Applicants should read that wording together with the detailed award list. The official page does not list a living allowance, monthly stipend, accommodation, meals, books, equipment, local transportation, visa costs, relocation expenses, or international travel as covered benefits. Candidates should not budget on the assumption that these unlisted costs will be paid. This distinction matters. The award offers strong academic-cost support, but it should not be described as an all-expenses-paid package unless AUC later publishes additional coverage in an individual award letter or updated terms. Applicants should prepare a personal budget for any expenses not expressly included and seek written clarification from AUC when necessary. Fellowship Duration and Continuation Conditions The award lasts for two semesters. Continued funding for the second semester is not unconditional: AUC reviews the fellow’s academic performance after the first semester and requires satisfactory progress. To retain the award, a recipient must maintain a minimum GPA of 3.2. This academic threshold should be treated as an ongoing condition, not simply an entry qualification. A fellow whose performance falls below the stated minimum may risk losing continued support. Recipients must also remain full-time students in the approved public policy or public administration graduate-diploma program and complete the required Public Policy HUB work. Because the academic and work obligations run together, candidates should assess whether they can realistically manage a full-time graduate course load alongside at least 12 working hours every week. Who Can Apply? The official eligibility rules identify two nationality or status groups: Egyptian nationals Refugees residing in Egypt who are Yemeni, Palestinian, Syrian, or Sudanese applicants The wording is specific. It does not announce eligibility for all nationalities, all refugees, all residents of Egypt, or all applicants from Africa or the Middle East. A refugee applicant must both reside in Egypt and fall within one of the four nationality groups named by AUC. The fellowship is intended for new graduate degree-seeking students who satisfy AUC’s full graduate admission requirements. AUC also refers to continuing students in the context of retaining the award and maintaining the required GPA. Prospective applicants should therefore understand the primary applicant profile as a new graduate student seeking admission, while the continuation rule governs recipients after the award begins. Academic and Admission Qualifications Fellowship eligibility and admission to AUC are connected but distinct. A candidate must be admissible to the relevant graduate program, and an admission offer does not by itself guarantee fellowship selection. At university level, AUC states that graduate applicants must hold an accredited bachelor’s degree and have an academic record sufficient for full or provisional admission. A specific department may impose additional or higher standards. Credentials must be submitted in English; documents issued in another language must be accompanied by an official English translation. For master’s and graduate-diploma admission consideration, AUC’s current general checklist includes: A completed online graduate application. Payment of the application fee online. Selection of up to two graduate programs for admission processing. A statement of purpose of approximately 500 words for each program selected, explaining the applicant’s interest, relevant skills or experience, and long-term academic and professional objectives. An updated curriculum vitae showing education and any work experience. At least two online recommendation letters from people familiar with the applicant’s academic or professional background. Official academic records, including the final detailed bachelor’s transcript and proof that the degree was completed. Depending on the case, an enrollment certificate or an equivalency certificate from Egypt’s Supreme Council of Universities may also be requested. Satisfactory English-language proficiency results. AUC notes that accepted tests can include the TOEFL iBT, Academic IELTS, and specified Cambridge English examinations, while individual programs may require higher scores. A clear valid national identity card for Egyptian applicants, or the information pages of a passport for international applicants and Egyptian dual nationals. One recent passport-size photograph in electronic form. Any additional requirements imposed by the selected program or requested for an individual case. Applicants should use the official AUC graduate admissions page as the controlling source for the complete and most current checklist. They should also review the selected diploma’s program-specific requirements before submission. A strong academic record is particularly important because the fellowship description expressly targets new graduate students with excellent academic performance. Responsibilities of Selected Fellows Receiving the award creates continuing obligations. According to AUC, every fellow must: Enroll full-time in the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration. Maintain a GPA of at least 3.2. Complete a minimum of 12 working hours per week with the Public Policy HUB. Respond to reporting requests from AUC by the deadlines communicated by the university. Supply requested materials that may include photographs or information about academic progress for reporting purposes. Attend fellowship meetings or events when requested by the relevant university units. Candidates should consider these conditions before applying. The 12-hour weekly commitment is substantial, particularly when combined with full-time graduate study. It may provide valuable policy experience, but it also requires dependable scheduling, professional conduct, timely communication, and consistent academic performance. Application Deadline for Spring and Fall 2027 The nearest published deadline is for the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle : Application opens: October 7, 2026 Application deadline: November 2, 2026 AUC also publishes two application cycles for Fall 2027 : Cycle 1 opens: December 22, 2026 Cycle 1 deadline: January 17, 2027 Cycle 2 opens: April 6, 2027 Cycle 2 deadline: May 6, 2027 These dates come from AUC’s fellowship deadline page, which was last updated on August 23, 2026. Applicants should recheck the official AUC fellowship deadlines immediately before submitting because universities may revise application calendars. The dates above concern the fellowship application cycle. Because AUC requires applicants to submit a graduate admission application as well as a fellowship application, candidates must also comply with any admission deadline applicable to their intended semester. Do not assume that finishing one form automatically completes the other process. How to Apply for the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development AUC describes a two-step application process. Both steps are essential. Step 1: Submit the AUC Graduate Admission Application Review the university’s graduate admission instructions and prepare the required documents. Then create an account or sign in through the AUC online application portal . Select the appropriate degree-seeking graduate-diploma program in public policy or public administration and complete every required section. Before submission, confirm that: The name and personal information on the application match the applicant’s official identity documents. Academic transcripts and proof of degree completion meet AUC’s official-document rules. Any document not issued in English has the required official translation. The statement of purpose is tailored to the selected program. Recommenders have enough time to submit their letters. English-proficiency results will remain valid through the first day of registered classes, as required by AUC. Step 2: Submit the Online Fellowship Application After addressing the graduate admission process, complete the separate fellowship application through the link provided on the official SFID listing . AUC’s fellowship button currently directs users to its Banner portal. Applicants should save confirmation pages or emails for both submissions. If the portals request different information, complete each form independently rather than assuming information transfers automatically between systems. How to Prepare a Strong Application The official page does not publish a detailed scoring rubric, so no applicant can guarantee selection. Nevertheless, candidates can present a clearer and more credible application by focusing on the qualities directly relevant to the fellowship’s stated design. 1. Demonstrate academic excellence with evidence The fellowship specifically targets applicants with excellent academic records. Use the CV, transcripts, statement of purpose, and recommendations to show consistent achievement, analytical ability, research experience, strong writing, or other evidence of readiness for graduate study. 2. Explain why the chosen diploma fits the applicant’s goals A generic statement is less useful than a focused explanation of why public policy or public administration is the appropriate field. Applicants should connect previous education, professional experience, volunteer work, research interests, or public-service ambitions to the diploma they select. 3. Show a credible interest in inclusive development Candidates can explain the social or policy challenges they hope to understand and address. The strongest discussion will be specific, grounded in experience, and connected to realistic academic and professional goals rather than relying on broad claims. 4. Address readiness for the Public Policy HUB commitment Because fellows must complete at least 12 working hours per week with the HUB, applicants should be ready to describe relevant strengths such as policy research, writing, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, communication, teamwork, or project coordination. They should also consider how they will balance this commitment with full-time study. 5. Choose recommenders strategically The general graduate checklist requires at least two recommendations. Suitable referees should know the applicant’s academic or professional work well enough to give concrete examples of performance, judgment, reliability, and potential for advanced study. 6. Start before the application window closes Official transcripts, English-language testing, translations, and recommendation letters can take time. Applicants should prepare these materials in advance and avoid treating the final day as the target submission date. Important Clarifications Before Applying Does the award fund a complete master’s degree? The fellowship provides full coverage for the credit hours needed for the eligible graduate diploma, up to nine credits per semester for two semesters. Diploma credits may count toward an MPP or MPA, but AUC does not state that this award covers the remaining requirements of either master’s degree. Is the fellowship open to applicants living outside Egypt? The official eligibility statement includes Egyptian nationals and refugees residing in Egypt from Yemen, Palestine, Syria, and Sudan. Refugee applicants should therefore not assume eligibility if they live outside Egypt. Can a refugee of any nationality apply? Not according to the published criteria. AUC expressly names Yemeni, Palestinian, Syrian, and Sudanese applicants among refugees residing in Egypt. Is a monthly stipend included? AUC’s published award list does not mention a stipend or living allowance. The listed support consists of eligible tuition, student services and activities fees, and medical service and health insurance fees. Is the award automatically renewed for the second semester? No. The two-semester duration is subject to review after the first semester for satisfactory academic performance, and fellows must maintain at least a 3.2 GPA. Is admission to AUC the same as receiving the fellowship? No. Candidates must complete the graduate admission application and the separate fellowship application. Admission eligibility is a requirement, while fellowship selection is a distinct funding decision. Where can applicants ask questions? AUC directs fellowship inquiries to gradserv@aucegypt.edu . Questions about unusual residency documentation, refugee status evidence, program-specific admission requirements, or unlisted expenses should be sent to AUC before the deadline. Final Application Checklist Before submitting, candidates should confirm that they have: Verified that they fall within one of the published nationality or refugee-status groups. Selected the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration. Reviewed AUC’s general and program-specific graduate admission requirements. Prepared an official bachelor’s transcript and proof of degree completion. Arranged an official English translation for any credential not issued in English. Prepared a focused statement of purpose of about 500 words for each selected program. Updated their CV. Requested at least two recommendation letters. Confirmed the applicable English-proficiency requirements and test validity. Completed the graduate admission application. Completed the separate fellowship application. Submitted both processes before their respective deadlines. Planned for a full-time course load and at least 12 Public Policy HUB working hours each week. Understood the minimum 3.2 GPA continuation requirement. Budgeted for expenses not identified in the official award coverage. Conclusion The Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at the American University in Cairo offers a focused route into graduate-level public policy or public administration study for academically excellent, eligible applicants. Its combination of tuition support, university fee coverage, health-related fee coverage, and practical work with the Public Policy HUB can help recipients develop both academic knowledge and applied policy experience. Applicants should approach the opportunity with a precise understanding of its scope. The award supports up to nine credits per semester for two semesters, requires full-time diploma enrollment, demands at least 12 hours of HUB work each week, and depends on maintaining a minimum 3.2 GPA. It is restricted to Egyptian nationals and specified refugee groups residing in Egypt, and it requires both an AUC graduate admission application and a separate fellowship application. For the Spring 2027 cycle, the fellowship application deadline is November 2, 2026. Prospective candidates should begin collecting academic records, recommendations, English-language evidence, and identity or residency documents well before the portal opens. All applicants should verify the current instructions and dates on AUC’s official website before submitting. For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: WMO Internship 2026 in Geneva: Paid Six-Month UN Opportunity in Partnerships, Climate and Resource Mobilization
summary: The World Meteorological Organization is accepting applications for a paid six-month internship in Geneva, Switzerland, within its Division of Development Partnerships and Programme Delivery. The placement offers an exceptional entry point into the United Nations system for a Master’s-level candidate interested in international partnerships, philanthropy, private-sector engagement, sustainable finance, climate action, resource mobilization, due diligence, strategic communications and high-level event coordination. The selected intern will join the Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit and work under the supervision of its Head. Rather than being limited to routine administrative support, the assignment covers partner research, meeting preparation, reputational-risk reviews, contributor engagement, briefing materials, knowledge management and support for major international platforms and events. Applications must be submitted through the official WMO recruitment portal by 22 September 2026 . The vacancy record is scheduled to close at 11:59 p.m. Geneva time . Candidates should apply early to avoid technical problems near the deadline. Full details are available on the official WMO vacancy page . WMO Internship 2026: Key Information Detail Information Host organization World Meteorological Organization Position Internship (INTERNSHIP-2026-DPPD 1) Job identification number 36754 Division Division of Development Partnerships and Programme Delivery Unit Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit Location Geneva, Switzerland Duration Six months Published Geneva stipend CHF 1,500 per month Experience No prior experience required Education Master’s level in a relevant field Required language Fluency in English Additional language French is advantageous Posting date 8 September 2026 Application deadline 22 September 2026 Application method WMO online e-recruitment system only The vacancy does not specify a starting date, number of openings, daily working schedule, relocation allowance or travel reimbursement. Applicants should not assume that costs not expressly covered by WMO’s published internship conditions will be paid. About the World Meteorological Organization The World Meteorological Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations and the UN system’s authoritative voice on weather, climate and water. WMO supports international cooperation in meteorology, climatology, operational hydrology and related geophysical sciences. It provides a framework through which its 193 Member States and Territories exchange Earth-system information and strengthen services that protect lives, livelihoods, economies and the environment. Its Secretariat is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Learn more about WMO’s mandate . This institutional environment makes the internship particularly relevant for candidates seeking to understand how a UN specialized agency develops partnerships beyond governments. The intern will gain exposure to WMO’s engagement with companies, foundations, investors, philanthropies, academic organizations and other non-state stakeholders. About the Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit The Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit operates within WMO’s Division of Development Partnerships and Programme Delivery. The Unit coordinates WMO’s institutional engagement with private and non-state actors, including: Private-sector companies; Philanthropic foundations and philanthropists; Commercial entities and technology companies; Business and industry associations; Investors and prospective contributors; High-net-worth individuals; and Other organizations capable of contributing finance, expertise, technology or in-kind resources. The Unit’s responsibility extends beyond identifying donors. It cultivates high-impact partnerships and supports WMO technical departments and Members in pursuing appropriate, mutually beneficial cooperation with external organizations. That work requires accurate research, effective relationship management, sound documentation, reputational safeguards and an understanding of WMO’s public-interest mandate. WMO describes public-private engagement as cooperation among public institutions, businesses, academia and civil society in producing and delivering weather, climate, hydrological, marine and environmental information and services. Its approach emphasizes public value, integrity, mutual benefit, transparency, sovereignty and sustainability. Read about WMO’s public-private engagement framework . The WMO Commons The WMO Commons is WMO’s pooled financing mechanism. According to the vacancy announcement, it aims to mobilize USD 100 million over five years . The intern will help the Unit identify potential contributors and strategic partners, conduct background research and maintain materials used for contributor and investor engagement. This work will provide practical experience in international resource mobilization, including: Identifying potential contributors; Understanding organizational funding priorities; Assessing strategic alignment; Preparing cases for support; Developing partner profiles; Updating pitch materials; and Recording and following up on engagement. The Open Consultative Platform The Open Consultative Platform is WMO’s principal mechanism for structured dialogue with private-sector and academic stakeholders. It supports discussion about partnerships, innovation and the future of the global weather, climate and water enterprise. The intern will assist with the preparation and follow-up of platform sessions and other high-level engagements. Assignments may include preparing concept notes, researching participants, developing agendas, compiling briefing packages, coordinating participation, recording meeting outcomes and monitoring follow-up actions. Why WMO Is Recruiting for This Placement The Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit is managing a growing portfolio connected with the WMO Commons, the Open Consultative Platform and wider partnership-development work. At the same time, the Unit is preparing for several prominent international engagements, including: TECO Amsterdam in October 2026; The fourth session of WMO’s Services Commission, known as SERCOM-4; COP31 in Antalya in November 2026; and The World Economic Forum in January 2027. The vacancy explains that the volume and complexity of these workstreams exceed the Unit’s current staffing capacity. The selected intern will provide operational support in research, meeting coordination, documentation, due diligence and communications. Candidates should therefore expect a fast-moving environment involving several simultaneous assignments and deadlines. Detailed Duties and Responsibilities 1. Partnership engagement and meeting support The intern will help coordinate bilateral meetings involving companies, philanthropic foundations, investors and other non-state actors. Responsibilities will include: Preparing meeting agendas; Researching organizations and participants; Developing background notes and participant profiles; Taking accurate meeting notes; Converting discussions into structured summaries; Recording decisions and agreed actions; Following up on outstanding actions; Updating the Dialogue Tracker; Maintaining contact lists; and Keeping partner-engagement records current. This area of work requires discretion, organization and the ability to distinguish significant decisions and action points from general discussion. 2. Partnership research and resource mobilization The intern will research and map prospective private-sector and philanthropic partners, contributors and funding opportunities. This will involve: Identifying organizations whose priorities may align with WMO’s work; Preparing institutional and partner profiles; Monitoring developments in philanthropy and sustainable finance; Researching private-sector engagement trends; Comparing prospective contributors and opportunities; Identifying potential areas of cooperation; and Supporting the prioritization of partnership and resource-mobilization opportunities. Candidates who can transform extensive research into short, decision-useful notes will be particularly well suited to this responsibility. 3. Due diligence and reputational-risk support Before engaging an external organization, WMO must consider integrity, compliance and reputational risks. The intern will assist by: Conducting background research on companies, foundations and other prospective partners; Reviewing relevant public information and databases; Supporting the preparation of due-diligence reviews; Assisting with reputational-risk assessments; Documenting the information used in each review; and Maintaining due-diligence records and trackers according to WMO procedures. This responsibility is especially relevant for applicants interested in governance, compliance, corporate responsibility, legal research, ESG, ethical partnership management or reputational-risk analysis. 4. Support for the WMO Commons The intern will contribute to the operationalization and promotion of the WMO Commons. Expected assignments include: Mapping prospective contributors and strategic partners; Researching potential sources of financial and in-kind support; Updating pitch materials; Preparing frequently asked questions; Developing presentations and communication products; and Compiling background information for investor and contributor discussions. The intern will learn how an international organization formulates a financing proposition and communicates it to different external audiences. 5. High-level event support The intern will support Open Consultative Platform sessions and other major private-sector and philanthropic engagements. Tasks may include: Drafting or updating concept notes; Supporting agenda development; Researching participants; Preparing briefing documents; Maintaining logistical documentation; Coordinating with participants; Producing meeting reports; and Tracking post-event actions. The placement is therefore relevant to candidates interested in multistakeholder dialogue, international conferences, diplomacy, stakeholder coordination or strategic event management. 6. Strategic platforms and sector engagement The intern will support WMO’s involvement in private-sector platforms, professional networks and global forums. These may cover: Sustainable finance; Climate risk; Technology and innovation; Weather and climate services; Water services; and International development priorities. The intern will monitor upcoming opportunities and prepare concise background papers or briefing materials as required. 7. Briefings, communications and knowledge management The intern will help prepare written materials for senior-level engagements, including: Official correspondence; Briefing notes; Talking points; Presentations; and Internal reports. The intern will also maintain organized records of the Unit’s partnerships and activities and support information exchange with other WMO units and technical departments. Additional related responsibilities may be assigned by the supervisor. Educational Requirements The vacancy calls for Master’s-level education in one of the following areas: International relations; International development; Climate studies; Business; Economics; Law or legal studies; or Another related discipline. WMO’s broader internship programme is intended for students and recent graduates. For this opening, candidates should be pursuing or have recently completed Master’s-level studies in a relevant field. Applicants must describe their current degree status accurately. Incomplete studies should not be presented as a completed qualification. Experience Requirements No prior professional experience is required. This allows candidates to use evidence from academic study, research assignments, dissertations, volunteering, student organizations or extracurricular activities. Academic exposure to the following subjects would be advantageous: International organizations; Private-sector engagement; Partnership development; Resource mobilization; Philanthropy; Sustainable finance; or Sustainability. Candidates should not avoid applying merely because they have never worked for the United Nations. The announcement expressly states that previous professional experience is not required. Required Skills Applicants should demonstrate: Strong research ability; Strong professional writing skills; Ability to work in a multicultural environment; Close attention to detail; and Ability to organize and manage multiple assignments simultaneously. The duties also indicate the practical value of analytical writing, reliable recordkeeping, stakeholder awareness, professional communication, sound judgment and disciplined follow-up. Language Requirements Fluency in English is mandatory. The assignment involves research, correspondence, meeting records, briefing notes, talking points, presentations and internal reports. Candidates should therefore be able to communicate clearly and accurately in professional English. Knowledge of French is advantageous but is not identified as a mandatory requirement. WMO’s general internship guidance also states that knowledge of another UN language—Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish—is desirable, although this particular vacancy specifically highlights French. Review the official WMO internship conditions . Learning and Professional Development The official vacancy identifies hands-on learning in public-private engagement at the international level. The selected intern can expect exposure to: Partnership development within a UN specialized agency; Private-sector and philanthropic engagement; Contributor research and resource mobilization; Due-diligence and reputational-risk processes; High-level meeting and event coordination; Strategic briefings and institutional communications; Stakeholder databases and knowledge-management systems; and Coordination among technical departments and external organizations. WMO’s general internship programme also aims to help participants: Understand WMO’s mandate; Learn applicable organizational rules and guidance; Develop an understanding of UN processes and policies; Complete mandatory training; Strengthen professional communication skills; Understand the challenges of working in a multicultural organization; and Build professional relationships and networks. Stipend, Leave and Insurance WMO’s published internship conditions state that interns recruited in Geneva receive CHF 1,500 per month . For a six-month placement, this would equal CHF 9,000 over the complete internship before considering any special institutional funding or insurance-related addition. Other published conditions include: If an intern is funded by a WMO Member State or university, the allowance follows the sending organization’s policy; Interns accrue 2.5 days of annual leave per month; A six-month appointment would therefore accrue 15 days of annual leave; Unused annual leave is not compensated when the internship ends; Health and accident insurance is mandatory for interns based in Switzerland; WMO recommends Swisscare for interns requiring sickness and accident insurance in Switzerland; The intern completes the enrollment, while WMO covers the expense by adding the insurance cost to the monthly stipend; Locally recruited interns who already have suitable insurance may opt out of Swisscare; Interns are covered by the WMO Benefits Insurance Plan and Malicious Act Insurance Policy; and If an intern is exceptionally required to travel for official work, accident and illness insurance applies to the travel. These are WMO’s general programme conditions. The selected candidate’s appointment letter will remain the controlling document for exact financial and insurance arrangements. Age, Diversity and Equal Opportunity The vacancy states that candidates must be at least 18 years old. It also mentions WMO’s statutory retirement age of 65 and requires an appointee to be able to complete the contract before reaching the mandatory age of separation. WMO is committed to diversity and a balanced workforce. Qualified women and men, including persons with disabilities, are encouraged to apply. No nationality, race, ethnicity or continental restriction is stated for this vacancy. WMO’s internship programme welcomes students and recent graduates from around the world. Its general internship guidance describes the programme’s potential audience as: Students approaching the end of their studies; Students who need an internship to complete their studies; Recent graduates; Early-career candidates with less than two years of relevant experience; Scholarship-supported interns; and Candidates sponsored by governments, NGOs or academic institutions. These general descriptions should be read together with the specific vacancy requirements, which state Master’s-level education, no prior experience requirement and a minimum age of 18. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through WMO’s online e-recruitment system. WMO does not accept applications by email or post. Candidates should follow these steps: Open the official vacancy page . Sign in to an existing candidate account or create a new profile. Complete all relevant profile sections, including education, language ability, academic projects and any work, volunteer or extracurricular experience. Demonstrate Master’s-level study in an eligible discipline. Provide evidence of research, writing, organization and multicultural teamwork. Review the profile for accuracy, completeness and consistency. Submit through the official portal only and avoid sending the application through multiple routes. Apply before 22 September 2026 , preferably well before the scheduled closing time. The public vacancy text does not prescribe a fixed package of supporting documents. Candidates should follow the document prompts presented inside the recruitment portal. WMO screens candidates using the information contained in their online profiles. Its official application guidance advises applicants to ensure that all information is complete and current before submission. Practical Tips for a Competitive Application These recommendations are based on the published responsibilities and are not additional eligibility conditions. Connect academic work to the assignment Candidates without extensive professional experience can use a thesis, capstone project, research paper or relevant coursework as evidence. Strong subject areas may include: Climate finance; Sustainable development; International organizations; Corporate responsibility; Philanthropy; Partnership models; Development economics; Compliance; or International law. Demonstrate decision-focused research Avoid merely stating that you possess research skills. Explain how you collected information, evaluated sources, identified risks or opportunities and converted findings into a clear output for a particular audience. Provide evidence of professional writing The role involves agendas, background notes, profiles, meeting summaries, briefing documents, talking points, presentations and reports. Highlight assignments or activities requiring accurate, concise and audience-appropriate writing. Show organization and follow-through The Unit needs support across several events and partnership workstreams. Provide an example of managing competing deadlines, maintaining records, coordinating participants or tracking actions through completion. Address due diligence and integrity Applicants with exposure to legal research, compliance, ESG, reputational-risk analysis, corporate governance or ethical screening should make that connection explicit. Academic experience can be relevant when it demonstrates careful evidence handling and balanced judgment. Highlight multicultural experience Evidence may come from international education, multicultural group projects, language learning, volunteer work, student associations or collaboration with people from different national and professional backgrounds. Candidates should state their actual proficiency and support it with education, certification or practical experience where possible.
